reviewedRevision: e7d7d365 (accepted build) plus the fixes in this commit
process: Lean final review at the user's request. The game already had 25 chambers, so it went straight to one independent review round. Its MEDIUM progress-store finding, a flat mastery tier and three cheap LOW items were fixed and verified by re-running the reviewer's own pilot, blind and correctness scripts, one clean-worktree run and the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: On the final files the reviewer's reaction-limited bot (public getState only, 60 Hz, 20 seeds per chamber) cleared 496 of 500 chamber runs at 0.35 s and 150 of 150 at 0.25 s. The worst chamber was 21 at 17 of 20, and the mastery chambers 17-25 now leave the machines at about 7-12 of 14 health against about 13 in the combination tier. The owner's 100-seed sweep found mastery at 98.2% at 0.35 s and 91.8% at 0.6 s, where it had been 249 of 250. Blind play (316 patterns per chamber: idle, mash, random keys, hold-and-alternate at 0.1-2 s) cleared 0.34% overall and at most 1.3% of any chamber from 3. Hostile dt and pointer fuzz found no problems, every broken progress store was safe, an X press was never lost at 30-240 Hz, and in the review round final states matched across 30, 60 and 120 Hz, each run ended exactly once and froze, and EN and ZH text fit.

findings.observation: Review finding: createGame and the chamber-clear unlock called env.progress without try/catch, so a throwing store crashed the game at start or at the first clear. Both calls are now guarded as in Shield Sentinel, with quality tests.

Review observation: mastery chambers 17-25 were longer but not harder; the reviewer's bot cleared every chamber with almost no damage, even at 0.6 s reaction. Mastery chambers now set a per-chamber tempo (0.5-0.65, faster wind-ups and walks) and plating (1-2 extra hit points per foe), and chamber 17's tip announces it.

Review findings: 'Ricochet Hall' had a tip about blocked throws and a corridor the bot could not aim in, the select screen marked cleared and current chambers by colour alone, and an X press could be lost on a frame with no simulation tick. The chamber is now 'Gap Hall' (缺口长厅) with split walls and a matching tip, cleared and current cells carry long and short bars, and X presses are queued until the next tick.

openNotes: The source is a single 1,600-line file, over the repository's 800-line soft ceiling; the review found no defect hidden by it.
Mastery is harder through faster, tougher foes and machine damage; the player's own HP is rarely threatened.
Several older quality gates that encoded the previous flat balance were relaxed, for example a casual bot now needs to reach chamber 17 rather than win all 25.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start and the language toggle; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: English: Start opened chamber 1 of 25 with HP, the weakest machine and the prompt 'Hold Space: pull · face foe, X: throw · dodge red' in the status line.
Loss: left idle, enemies wound up on the machine until 'Machine 1 hit! 0/14', and the run ended with 'One more try?' and 'Enemies wrecked the machinery. Hit them before their wind-up ends.'
Chinese 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): chamber 1 in Chinese with touch buttons 左, 上, 下, 右, 吸引（按住） and 排斥.
Not covered in the browser: a chamber win and the mastery chambers; the reviewer's pilot and the quality tests cover them.
